Ігнорувати відмову — втрата дрона.
items.tips: Не панікуй. Плануй на ціль. Май резервний дрон.

items.name: Пожежа акумулятора
items.desc: Не гаси водою. Використовуй пісок або вогнестійкий пакет.
items.why: Пожежа акумулятора — це «небезпека» для оператора. Вона захищає від вибуху. Вона ефективна для безпеки.
items.example: Дрон впав, акумулятор пошкоджений і почав диміти. Оператор кидає його в пісок і накриває. Через 5 хвилин дим припиняється.
mistakes: Гасити водою — вибух і розліт іскор.
Тримати пошкоджений акумулятор у кишені — пожежа на тілі.
Залишати акумулятор без нагляду — займається через 10–30 хвилин.
items.tips: Завжди май під рукою пісок або вогнестійкий пакет. Пошкоджений акумулятор — у пісок, на відкрите повітря, подалі від людей. Не залишай без нагляду 30 хвилин.

items.name: FPV
items.desc: Kamikaze drone with video goggles. The operator controls it in first person, as if sitting in the cockpit. High maneuverability, precision, low cost.
items.why: FPV is the main weapon of close combat. Cheap ($300–2000), expendable, and able to fly into a trench, bunker, or tank hatch. That is why FPVs became mass-produced.
items.example: The operator sees an enemy APC hiding behind a building. He flies the drone around the corner, sees the vehicle from behind, and dives into the open hatch. Explosion — APC destroyed. Cost: ~$500.
mistakes: Flying in a straight line — EW or an interceptor will take you down.
Ignoring altitude — at low altitude the drone snags on branches and wires.
Forgetting a backup frequency — the main channel is jammed, and the drone is lost.
items.tips: Keep the drone moving, never hover in one spot. Attack from an unexpected angle. Always have a backup frequency and a spare battery.

items.name: Bomber
items.desc: Bomber drone. Lifts munitions (grenades, mines) and drops them from altitude on positions (Mavic, Vampire, Baba Yaga). Works on areas and shelters.
items.why: A bomber does not expend itself on a strike — it returns and drops again. One drone can make 5–10 sorties per day. This is cost-effective for hitting trenches, bunkers, and infantry clusters.
items.example: Baba Yaga (heavy bomber) lifts 4 mines and drops them on an enemy trench. After the drop it returns, recharges, and flies again. In a day — 6 sorties, 24 mines.
mistakes: Dropping from low altitude — you will be seen and shot down.
Dropping without wind correction — the munition drifts off target.
Flying the same route — the enemy will set an ambush.
items.tips: Drop from 100–150 m with wind correction. Change routes. Use a thermal imager for night drops.

items.name: Recon
items.desc: Reconnaissance UAV (Shark, Leleka, Furia). Flies high, sees far, corrects artillery. The brigade's eyes.
items.why: A recon drone does not shoot, but without it artillery fires blindly. It provides coordinates, adjusts fire, and assesses results. One recon drone replaces a dozen observers.
items.example: Shark climbs to 1500 m, spots a vehicle column 30 km away, transmits coordinates. Artillery covers the column. The recon drone adjusts: 'left 50, further 100' — and confirms the kill.
mistakes: Flying low — you will be shot down by MANPADS or an interceptor.
Transmitting coordinates without accuracy — artillery will miss.
Forgetting about EW — GPS is jammed, and coordinates become inaccurate.
items.tips: Fly high (1000+ m). Transmit coordinates with 10 m accuracy. Keep a backup comm channel. Use optics with good resolution.

items.name: Loitering
items.desc: Flies along a route, finds a target and attacks (Lancet, Shahed). Can circle over a target for a long time waiting for the moment to strike.
items.why: A loitering drone is a 'smart mine in the air'. It does not just fly to a point — it searches for a target, waits, and attacks when convenient. Lancet can loiter for 40–60 minutes.
items.example: A Lancet is launched toward an enemy column. It circles over the road for 30 minutes until a tank appears. It dives and strikes. A regular kamikaze would have hit an empty road.
mistakes: Launching without recon — the drone will circle in vain and fall.
Ignoring EW — Lancet is jammed and loses the target.
No backup channel — loss of comms means loss of the drone.
items.tips: Launch after recon — know where the target is. Keep a backup channel. Use optics to search for the target. Do not launch in a strong EW zone.

items.name: Interceptor
items.desc: Shoots down other drones in the air by ramming or explosion (Sting, P1-SUN). Used for air defense.
items.why: An interceptor is a cheap alternative to SAM. A missile costs $100k+, an interceptor — $2–5k. It rams an enemy drone and destroys it. This is cost-effective against mass attacks.
items.example: An enemy Shahed flies toward a city. A Sting interceptor climbs, catches up, and rams it. Both drones fall. Cost: $3k instead of $100k for a missile.
mistakes: Ramming from close range — the explosion will damage the interceptor too.
Not accounting for speed — Shahed is faster than it looks.
Flying without battery reserve — you will not catch the target.
items.tips: Ram with a slight speed advantage. Keep 30% battery reserve. Work in pairs — one distracts, the other rams.

items.name: EW
items.desc: Electronic Warfare. Jams GPS, video, control. The main threat to any UAV.
items.why: EW is an invisible enemy. It does not shoot, but jams the signal, and the drone loses orientation. Without understanding EW, the operator does not know why the drone behaves strangely.
items.example: An FPV flies to the target, suddenly video disappears and the drone starts circling. EW is jamming the video channel. The operator switches frequency — video returns.
mistakes: Thinking EW jams everything — it jams specific frequencies.
No backup frequency — jamming the main one means losing the drone.
Flying in an EW zone without a plan — the drone is lost.
items.tips: Know the EW frequencies in the area. Have 2–3 backup frequencies. Use EW-resistant systems (6+ GHz, INS).

items.name: Radar
items.desc: Radio detection station. Detects objects at range by reflecting radio waves. Sees metal well, plastic poorly.
items.why: Radar is the eyes of air defense. It sees a drone at 5–50 km depending on RCS. The smaller the RCS, the later you are detected.
items.example: An FPV with RCS 0.005 m² is seen by radar at 3–5 km. A large Shahed with RCS 2 m² — at 30–50 km. That is why FPV sneaks in unnoticed, while Shahed is seen in advance.
mistakes: Thinking radar sees everything — it sees metal, plastic poorly.
Ignoring radar — you will be detected and shot down.
Flying low — radar does not see you, but optics do.
items.tips: Reduce RCS: plastic body, concealed antennas. Fly low to avoid radar. But remember: optics and acoustics will still find you.

items.name: RCS
items.desc: Radar Cross Section. The smaller — the harder to detect the drone on radar.
items.why: RCS is what radar sees. Mavic has RCS ~0.01 m², FPV — ~0.005 m², a large drone — 1–5 m². The smaller the RCS, the later you are detected and the less time the enemy has to react.
items.example: An FPV with RCS 0.005 m² is seen by radar at 3–5 km. A large Shahed with RCS 2 m² — at 30–50 km. That is why FPV sneaks in unnoticed, while Shahed is seen in advance.
mistakes: Thinking low RCS = invisibility — optics and acoustics still see you.
Flying with metal parts that increase RCS.
items.tips: Reduce RCS: plastic body, concealed antennas, avoid metal protrusions. But remember: EW and optics will still find you.

items.name: CEP
items.desc: Circular Error Probable. Accuracy indicator: the smaller — the more precise.
items.why: CEP is the language of artillerymen and developers. If CEP is 5 m, it means half of hits fall within a 5 m radius circle. For FPV, CEP is effectively 0–1 m (the operator sees the target), for Shahed — 5–30 m (inertial navigation), for ballistics — 100–300 m.
items.example: The commander says: 'Target — depot, CEP 10 m.' The operator understands: the drone may miss by 10 m, so it is better to approach from a side where there are no friendlies. If CEP is 1 m — you can hit the door precisely.
mistakes: Confusing CEP with blast radius — they are different things.
Believing CEP 0 means 100% hit — it is statistics, not a guarantee.
items.tips: Ask for CEP before a strike. If CEP is larger than the target size — correction or a different munition is needed.

items.name: INS
items.desc: Inertial Navigation System. Allows flying without GPS — by gyroscopes and accelerometers. EW-resistant, but accumulates error over time.
items.why: INS is the drone's 'memory' of where it is. When GPS is jammed, INS keeps guiding the drone by inertia. But error accumulates: 1 km per 10 minutes of flight.
items.example: A Shahed flies 1000 km. GPS is jammed for 200 km. INS guides the drone further, but error accumulates — 5–10 km. That is why Shahed often misses large targets.
mistakes: Thinking INS is precise — it accumulates error.
Not calibrating INS before flight — error is larger.
Flying long without correction — error becomes critical.
items.tips: Calibrate INS before flight. Use optical (DSMAC) or terrain correction. Plan shorter distances when GPS is jammed.

items.name: GNSS
items.desc: Global Navigation Satellite System (GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou). Gives precise coordinates, but is easily jammed.
items.why: GNSS is the drone's 'eye' that sees satellites. It gives precise coordinates (1–5 m), but is jammed by EW. Without GNSS the drone switches to INS.
items.example: An FPV flies to the target, GPS is jammed. The drone switches to INS and continues flight, but error accumulates. The operator corrects by video.
mistakes: Thinking GPS is always available — it gets jammed.
No INS — without GPS the drone will fall.
Ignoring GPS error — it can be 10–30 m.
items.tips: Keep INS as backup. Calibrate GPS before flight. Use multiple systems (GPS + GLONASS + Galileo) for accuracy.

items.name: RTH
items.desc: Return to Home — automatic return to the launch point. Triggers on loss of comms or by command.
items.why: RTH is the drone's 'insurance'. If comms are lost, the drone flies home by itself. Without RTH the drone flies who-knows-where and falls.
items.example: An FPV flies to the target, suddenly comms disappear. The drone switches to RTH and flies to the launch point. The operator finds it on the ground.
mistakes: Not configuring RTH — the drone flies who-knows-where.
Configuring RTH to the wrong point — the drone flies to the enemy.
Ignoring RTH altitude — the drone may hit a tree.
items.tips: Set RTH to the launch point. Set RTH altitude above obstacles. Check RTH before flight.

items.name: Failsafe
items.desc: Protective behavior on loss of signal: hover, return, or land. Configured in advance.
items.why: Failsafe is the drone's 'plan B'. If signal is lost, the drone must know what to do. Without failsafe the drone simply falls.
items.example: An FPV flies, comms disappear. Failsafe is set to RTH — the drone flies home. If failsafe were 'land' — the drone would land in a field.
mistakes: Not configuring failsafe — the drone falls.
Configuring failsafe to 'land' in a forest — the drone gets stuck.
Ignoring failsafe — loss of the drone.
items.tips: Set failsafe to RTH. Check failsafe before flight. Keep a backup comm channel.

items.name: Waypoint
items.desc: A route point. The drone flies through set points automatically, without operator input.
items.why: Waypoint is the drone's 'autopilot'. It flies through points while the operator observes. This allows long missions without constant control.
items.example: A recon drone flies through 10 points, recording video at each. The operator only observes and adjusts the route.
mistakes: Forgetting obstacles — the drone hits a tree.
Not checking the route — the drone flies to the enemy.
Ignoring wind — the drone drifts off route.
items.tips: Plan the route with obstacles in mind. Check the route on a map. Have a backup route.

items.name: Micro
items.desc: Up to 2 kg. Mavic, FPV, short-range recon. Hand launch, short range, quiet.
items.why: Micro drones are the 'infantry' of the air. They are cheap, mass-produced, expendable. They work at the front line, at 1–10 km.
items.example: An FPV is hand-launched by a soldier in a trench. It flies 2 km to an enemy position and strikes a machine gunner. Cost: $500.
mistakes: Launching from open terrain — you will be seen.
Flying too far — battery will not last.
Ignoring wind — a light drone drifts.
items.tips: Launch from cover. Fly 1–5 km. Keep a spare battery. Use quiet modes.

items.name: Mini
items.desc: 2–10 kg. Leleka, Shark, Furia. Catapult launch, tactical range.
items.why: Mini drones are 'tactical recon'. They fly 10–50 km, see far, correct artillery. They are more expensive than micro but more effective.
items.example: A Leleka is catapult-launched. It flies 30 km, spots a vehicle column, transmits coordinates. Artillery covers the column.
mistakes: Launching without a catapult — the drone will not take off.
Flying low — you will be shot down.
Ignoring EW — GPS is jammed.
items.tips: Use a catapult. Fly high (1000+ m). Keep a backup channel. Use optics with good resolution.

items.name: Medium
items.desc: 10–50 kg. PD-2, Raybird. Operational range, long reconnaissance.
items.why: Medium drones are 'operational recon'. They fly 50–200 km and can stay airborne 10–20 hours. They are expensive but effective.
items.example: A Raybird flies 150 km, spots an enemy base, transmits coordinates. Artillery covers the base. The drone returns.
mistakes: Flying without a plan — the drone wastes battery.
Ignoring weather — the drone will not withstand wind.
No backup channel — loss of comms.
items.tips: Plan the route. Fly in good weather. Keep a backup channel. Use satellite comms.

items.name: Large
items.desc: 50–200 kg. Bayraktar TB2, UJ-22. Operational-strategic range, strike missions.
items.why: Large drones are 'strategic recon and strike'. They fly 200–1000 km and can carry munitions. They are expensive but effective.
items.example: A Bayraktar TB2 flies 300 km, spots an enemy column, strikes it with a missile. Returns to base.
mistakes: Flying without air defense — you will be shot down.
Ignoring EW — GPS is jammed.
No plan — the drone wastes fuel.
items.tips: Fly with air defense. Keep a backup channel. Plan the route. Use satellite comms.

items.name: Strategic
items.desc: Over 200 kg. Tu-141, Palianytsia. Strikes on deep rear.
items.why: Strategic drones are 'strikes on the rear'. They fly 1000+ km and carry large munitions. They are expensive but effective.
items.example: A Tu-141 flies 1000 km, strikes an enemy depot. Returns or explodes.
mistakes: Flying without a plan — the drone wastes fuel.
Ignoring air defense — you will be shot down.
No backup channel — loss of comms.
items.tips: Plan the route. Fly with air defense. Keep a backup channel. Use satellite comms.

items.name: Short Range
items.desc: Up to 10 km. FPV, Mavic. Tactical level, battlefield, trench.
items.why: Short range is the 'battlefield'. Drones work at 1–10 km, within line of sight. They are cheap, mass-produced, expendable.
items.example: An FPV is launched from a trench, flies 2 km to an enemy position and strikes a machine gunner. Cost: $500.
mistakes: Flying too far — battery will not last.
Ignoring EW — jamming.
Launching from open terrain — you will be seen.
items.tips: Fly 1–5 km. Keep a spare battery. Use quiet modes. Launch from cover.

items.name: Tactical
items.desc: 10–50 km. Leleka, Shark. Brigade level, artillery coordination.
items.why: Tactical range is the 'brigade level'. Drones work at 10–50 km, correct artillery, conduct recon. They are more expensive than FPV but more effective.
items.example: A Leleka flies 30 km, spots a vehicle column, transmits coordinates. Artillery covers the column.
mistakes: Flying low — you will be shot down.
Ignoring EW — GPS is jammed.
No backup channel — loss of comms.
items.tips: Fly high (1000+ m). Keep a backup channel. Use optics with good resolution.

items.name: Operational
items.desc: 50–200 km. PD-2, Raybird. Operational level, deep reconnaissance.
items.why: Operational range is the 'operational level'. Drones work at 50–200 km, conduct deep recon. They are expensive but effective.
items.example: A Raybird flies 150 km, spots an enemy base, transmits coordinates. Artillery covers the base.
mistakes: Flying without a plan — the drone wastes battery.
Ignoring weather — the drone will not withstand wind.
No backup channel — loss of comms.
items.tips: Plan the route. Fly in good weather. Keep a backup channel. Use satellite comms.

items.name: Operational-Strategic
items.desc: 200–1000 km. UJ-22, Liutyi. Deep rear, infrastructure strikes.
items.why: Operational-strategic range is the 'deep rear'. Drones work at 200–1000 km, strike infrastructure. They are expensive but effective.
items.example: A UJ-22 flies 500 km, strikes an enemy depot. Returns or explodes.
mistakes: Flying without a plan — the drone wastes fuel.
Ignoring air defense — you will be shot down.
No backup channel — loss of comms.
items.tips: Plan the route. Fly with air defense. Keep a backup channel. Use satellite comms.

items.name: Strategic
items.desc: Over 1000 km. Tu-141, Palianytsia. Strategic level.
items.why: Strategic range is the 'strategic level'. Drones work at 1000+ km, strike strategic targets. They are expensive but effective.
items.example: A Tu-141 flies 1000 km, strikes an enemy depot. Returns or explodes.
mistakes: Flying without a plan — the drone wastes fuel.
Ignoring air defense — you will be shot down.
No backup channel — loss of comms.
items.tips: Plan the route. Fly with air defense. Keep a backup channel. Use satellite comms.

items.name: HE-Frag (OF)
items.desc: Universal. Strikes personnel and light equipment with fragments and shock wave. Most common.
items.why: HE-Frag is the 'universal' warhead. It works on everything: infantry, light equipment, shelters. It is cheap and mass-produced.
items.example: An FPV with HE-Frag strikes an enemy trench. Fragments kill 2–3 soldiers. Cost: $500.
mistakes: Using against a tank — will not penetrate armor.
Dropping from low altitude — fragments scatter.
Ignoring wind — fragments drift.
items.tips: Use against infantry and light equipment. Drop from 100+ m. Account for wind.

items.name: Cumulative (HEAT)
items.desc: Against armor. Creates a narrow jet that penetrates armor. Works well on tanks and APCs.
items.why: HEAT is the 'anti-tank' warhead. It creates a narrow metal jet that penetrates armor. It is effective against tanks and APCs.
items.example: An FPV with HEAT strikes an enemy tank. The jet penetrates armor, the tank explodes. Cost: $800.
mistakes: Using against infantry — few fragments.
Dropping from low altitude — the jet does not form.
Ignoring ERA — HEAT will not penetrate.
items.tips: Use against tanks and APCs. Drop from 100+ m. Account for ERA (use a tandem warhead).

items.name: Tandem
items.desc: Two warheads: first removes ERA, second penetrates main armor. Against modern tanks.
items.why: Tandem is 'against modern tanks'. The first warhead removes ERA, the second penetrates main armor. It is effective against tanks with ERA.
items.example: An FPV with a tandem warhead strikes a modern tank. The first warhead removes ERA, the second penetrates armor. The tank explodes. Cost: $1500.
mistakes: Using against infantry — few fragments.
Dropping from low altitude — warheads do not form.
Ignoring distance — warheads detonate at different times.
items.tips: Use against modern tanks. Drop from 100+ m. Account for the distance between warheads.

items.name: Thermobaric
items.desc: Against shelters. Explosion with lots of heat and pressure, burns oxygen. Effective in trenches and basements.
items.why: Thermobaric is 'against shelters'. It creates an explosion with lots of heat and pressure, burns oxygen. It is effective in trenches, basements, bunkers.
items.example: An FPV with a thermobaric warhead strikes an enemy bunker. The explosion burns oxygen, everyone inside dies. Cost: $1000.
mistakes: Using in open terrain — little effect.
Dropping from low altitude — the explosion does not form.
Ignoring wind — heat drifts.
items.tips: Use against shelters. Drop from 100+ m. Account for wind.

items.name: Incendiary
items.desc: Against depots. Causes fires, destroys material stocks.
items.why: Incendiary is 'against depots'. It causes fires, destroys material stocks. It is effective against depots, fuel tanks, equipment.
items.example: An FPV with an incendiary warhead strikes an enemy fuel depot. The fire destroys 10 tons of fuel. Cost: $700.
mistakes: Using against infantry — little effect.
Dropping from low altitude — the fire does not spread.
Ignoring wind — the fire drifts.
items.tips: Use against depots. Drop from 100+ m. Account for wind.

items.name: Cluster
items.desc: Against areas. Scatters submunitions over a large territory.
items.why: Cluster is 'against areas'. It scatters submunitions over a large territory. It is effective against infantry clusters, equipment, airfields.
items.example: An FPV with a cluster warhead strikes an enemy airfield. Submunitions destroy 3 aircraft. Cost: $2000.
mistakes: Using against a single target — little effect.
Dropping from low altitude — submunitions do not scatter.
Ignoring wind — submunitions drift.
items.tips: Use against areas. Drop from 200+ m. Account for wind.

items.name: EFP (Strike Core)
items.desc: Against light armor. Forms a compact metal core that penetrates armor.
items.why: EFP is 'against light armor'. It forms a compact metal core that penetrates armor. It is effective against APCs, IFVs, light tanks.
items.example: An FPV with an EFP warhead strikes an enemy APC. The core penetrates armor, the APC explodes. Cost: $900.
mistakes: Using against heavy tanks — will not penetrate.
Dropping from low altitude — the core does not form.
Ignoring distance — the core disperses.
items.tips: Use against light armor. Drop from 100+ m. Account for distance.

items.name: Inertial (INS)
items.desc: Without GPS. Works by gyroscopes. EW-resistant, but has accumulating error.
items.why: INS is the drone's 'memory' of where it is. When GPS is jammed, INS keeps guiding the drone by inertia. But error accumulates: 1 km per 10 minutes of flight. The longer the flight — the larger the error.
items.example: A Shahed flies 1000 km. GPS is jammed for 200 km. INS guides the drone further, but error accumulates — 5–10 km. That is why Shahed often misses large targets.
mistakes: Thinking INS is precise — it accumulates error.
Not calibrating INS before flight — error is larger.
Flying long without correction — error becomes critical.
items.tips: Calibrate INS before flight. Use optical (DSMAC) or terrain correction. Plan shorter distances when GPS is jammed.

items.name: Satellite (GPS/GLONASS)
items.desc: Precise, but vulnerable to EW. Easily jammed — then the drone switches to INS.
items.why: Satellite navigation is the drone's 'eye' that sees satellites. It gives precise coordinates (1–5 m), but is jammed by EW. Without GPS the drone switches to INS.
items.example: An FPV flies to the target, GPS is jammed. The drone switches to INS and continues flight, but error accumulates. The operator corrects by video.
mistakes: Thinking GPS is always available — it gets jammed.
No INS — without GPS the drone will fall.
Ignoring GPS error — it can be 10–30 m.
items.tips: Keep INS as backup. Calibrate GPS before flight. Use multiple systems (GPS + GLONASS + Galileo) for accuracy.

items.name: Optical (DSMAC)
items.desc: By terrain. Compares images with reference. EW-resistant.
items.why: DSMAC is the drone's 'photo memory'. It compares the current terrain image with a reference and corrects course. It is EW-resistant but requires good visibility.
items.example: A Tomahawk flies 1500 km. At the end of the flight DSMAC compares the terrain image with the reference and corrects course. Error: 10–30 m.
mistakes: Using at night — optics cannot see.
Using in fog — optics cannot see.
No reference — DSMAC does not work.
items.tips: Use by day and in good weather. Keep a reference image. Combine with INS for reliability.

items.name: Thermal (IR)
items.desc: By temperature. Works at night and in bad weather.
items.why: IR is the drone's 'thermal eye'. It sees heat, so it works at night, in smoke, through light vegetation. It is effective against equipment and infantry.
items.example: An FPV with IR guidance strikes an enemy tank at night. The thermal imager sees the engine, the drone approaches from behind and strikes.
mistakes: Using by day — heat dissipates.
Ignoring camouflage — thermal sees through it.
No cooling — IR sensor overheats.
items.tips: Use at night and in bad weather. Keep cooling. Combine with a day camera.

items.name: Laser
items.desc: Target illumination by laser. Requires operator with laser designator.
items.why: Laser is 'precision guidance'. It requires an operator with a laser designator to illuminate the target. It is effective against point targets.
items.example: The operator illuminates an enemy tank with a laser. An FPV with laser guidance flies to the illuminated target and strikes it.
mistakes: Illuminating without coordination — the drone flies wrong.
Illuminating from close range — you will be seen.
Ignoring weather — the laser scatters.
items.tips: Coordinate with the operator. Illuminate from afar. Account for weather.

items.name: Radar (ARH)
items.desc: By radio contrast. Works on metal objects (ships, tanks).
items.why: ARH is the drone's 'radar eye'. It sees metal, so it works on ships, tanks, APCs. It is effective against large metal targets.
items.example: An anti-ship missile with ARH flies to a ship. The radar sees metal, the missile strikes the ship.
mistakes: Using against infantry — radar does not see.
Ignoring EW — radar is jammed.
No backup guidance — radar may fail.
items.tips: Use against metal targets. Keep backup guidance. Account for EW.

items.name: Computer Vision (AI)
items.desc: Object recognition. Modern drones find the target by silhouette themselves even without comms.
items.why: AI is the drone's 'brain'. It recognizes objects by silhouette, so the drone finds the target even without comms. It is effective against mass attacks.
items.example: An FPV with AI guidance flies to the target. The operator loses comms, but the drone finds the tank by silhouette and strikes it.
mistakes: Thinking AI always works — it makes mistakes.
Not training AI — it does not recognize the target.
Ignoring AI errors — the drone may hit friendlies.
items.tips: Train AI on real targets. Keep backup guidance. Check AI before flight.

items.name: Electric
items.desc: Quiet, but short range. FPV, Mavic, light recon. Powered by battery.
items.why: An electric engine is a 'quiet' engine. It does not make noise, so the drone is hard to detect by sound. But it has short range (10–30 minutes).
items.example: An FPV with an electric engine flies 2 km, strikes the target, and returns. Flight time: 15 minutes.
mistakes: Flying too far — battery will not last.
Ignoring cold — battery drains faster.
No spare battery — the drone falls.
items.tips: Fly 1–10 km. Keep a spare battery. Keep the battery warm.

items.name: Piston (ICE)
items.desc: Long range. Shahed, Leleka (some), Raybird. Runs on gasoline.
items.why: A piston engine is a 'long-range' engine. It runs on gasoline, so the drone can fly 10–20 hours. It is effective for long-range recon and strikes.
items.example: A Shahed with a piston engine flies 1000 km, strikes the target. Flight time: 10 hours.
mistakes: Ignoring fuel — the drone falls.
No fuel reserve — the drone will not reach.
Ignoring noise — you will be heard.
items.tips: Plan fuel. Keep a reserve. Fly high so you are not heard.

items.name: Turbojet
items.desc: High speed. UJ-25, Palianytsia, missiles.
items.why: A turbojet engine is a 'fast' engine. It gives high speed (500–900 km/h), so the drone is hard to intercept. It is effective for strikes on deep rear.
items.example: A UJ-25 with a turbojet engine flies 500 km/h, strikes the target. Flight time: 1 hour.
mistakes: Ignoring fuel — the drone falls.
No fuel reserve — the drone will not reach.
Ignoring noise — you will be heard.
items.tips: Plan fuel. Keep a reserve. Fly high so you are not heard.

items.name: Turboprop
items.desc: Economical at long distances. Bayraktar TB2, strategic UAVs.
items.why: A turboprop engine is an 'economical' engine. It is economical at long distances, so the drone can fly 20–30 hours. It is effective for strategic recon.
items.example: A Bayraktar TB2 with a turboprop engine flies 24 hours, conducts recon. Flight time: 24 hours.
mistakes: Ignoring fuel — the drone falls.
No fuel reserve — the drone will not reach.
Ignoring noise — you will be heard.
items.tips: Plan fuel. Keep a reserve. Fly high so you are not heard.

items.name: Pulsejet
items.desc: Cheap, but loud. Trembita, Iranian missiles.
items.why: A pulsejet engine is a 'cheap' engine. It is cheap but loud. It is effective for mass attacks.
items.example: A Trembita with a pulsejet engine flies 200 km, strikes the target. Cost: $3000.
mistakes: Ignoring noise — you will be heard.
No fuel reserve — the drone falls.
Ignoring accuracy — the drone misses.
items.tips: Fly low so you are not heard. Keep a fuel reserve. Account for accuracy.

items.name: Solid-fuel (SRM)
items.desc: Missiles. Ballistic, anti-air, anti-tank.
items.why: A solid-fuel engine is a 'rocket' engine. It gives high speed (1000+ km/h), so the missile is hard to intercept. It is effective for ballistic, anti-air, anti-tank missiles.
items.example: A ballistic missile with SRM flies 1000 km/h, strikes the target. Flight time: 5 minutes.
mistakes: Ignoring accuracy — the missile misses.
No backup guidance — the missile falls.
Ignoring air defense — the missile is shot down.
items.tips: Account for accuracy. Keep backup guidance. Fly high so you are not shot down.

items.name: Hand Launch
items.desc: Light drones (up to 5 kg). Operator runs and throws.
items.why: Hand launch is a 'simple' method. It requires no equipment, so it is fast. It is effective for light drones (FPV, Mavic).
items.example: An FPV is hand-launched by a soldier in a trench. It flies 2 km to an enemy position and strikes a machine gunner.
mistakes: Throwing against the wind — the drone falls.
Throwing from low altitude — the drone hits the ground.
Throwing without a run-up — the drone does not take off.
items.tips: Throw with the wind. Throw from 1.5–2 m. Run up before throwing.

items.name: Catapult
items.desc: Medium drones (5–20 kg). Rubber, pneumatic or mechanical.
items.why: A catapult is a 'mechanical' method. It gives the drone initial speed, so it takes off. It is effective for medium drones (Leleka, Shark).
items.example: A Leleka is catapult-launched. It flies 30 km, spots a vehicle column, transmits coordinates.
mistakes: Launching without a check — the drone falls.
Launching against the wind — the drone falls.
Launching from low altitude — the drone hits the ground.
items.tips: Check the catapult. Launch with the wind. Launch from 2–3 m.

items.name: Rail
items.desc: Heavy drones. Launch along guide with booster.
items.why: A rail is a 'guide' method. It gives the drone initial speed, so it takes off. It is effective for heavy drones.
items.example: A heavy drone is rail-launched. It flies 500 km, strikes the target.
mistakes: Launching without a check — the drone falls.
Launching against the wind — the drone falls.
Launching from low altitude — the drone hits the ground.
items.tips: Check the rail. Launch with the wind. Launch from 3–5 m.

items.name: Runway
items.desc: Aircraft-type drones. Requires flat surface (asphalt, ground).
items.why: A runway is an 'aircraft' method. It gives the drone initial speed, so it takes off. It is effective for aircraft-type drones (Bayraktar TB2).
items.example: A Bayraktar TB2 takes off from a runway. It flies 24 hours, conducts recon.
mistakes: Taking off from uneven surface — the drone falls.
Taking off against the wind — the drone falls.
Taking off without a check — the drone falls.
items.tips: Use a flat surface. Take off with the wind. Check the drone before takeoff.

items.name: Container (TLC)
items.desc: Missiles. Launch from transport-launch container.
items.why: A container is a 'rocket' method. It gives the missile initial speed, so it takes off. It is effective for missiles.
items.example: A missile is launched from a TLC. It flies 1000 km, strikes the target.
mistakes: Launching without a check — the missile falls.
Launching against the wind — the missile falls.
Launching from low altitude — the missile hits the ground.
items.tips: Check the TLC. Launch with the wind. Launch from 3–5 m.

items.name: Air Launch
items.desc: From aircraft or helicopter. For large missiles and drones.
items.why: Air launch is an 'air' method. It gives the missile initial speed, so it takes off. It is effective for large missiles and drones.
items.example: A missile is air-launched from an aircraft. It flies 1000 km, strikes the target.
mistakes: Launching without a check — the missile falls.
Launching against the wind — the missile falls.
Launching from low altitude — the missile hits the ground.
items.tips: Check the missile. Launch with the wind. Launch from 5–10 km.

items.name: Belly Landing
items.desc: Light drones. Land on belly, often with parachute.
items.why: Belly landing is a 'simple' method. It requires no landing gear, so it is light. It is effective for light drones.
items.example: An FPV lands on its belly in a field. It is undamaged and can be launched again.
mistakes: Landing on hard surface — the drone is damaged.
Landing against the wind — the drone flips.
Landing without a parachute — the drone crashes.
items.tips: Land on soft surface. Land with the wind. Use a parachute.

items.name: Parachute
items.desc: Standard for most UAVs. Safe, but requires space.
items.why: A parachute is a 'safe' method. It gives the drone a soft landing, so it is not damaged. It is effective for most UAVs.
items.example: A Leleka lands by parachute. It is undamaged and can be launched again.
mistakes: Landing on hard surface — the drone is damaged.
Landing against the wind — the drone flips.
Landing without a check — the parachute does not open.
items.tips: Land on soft surface. Land with the wind. Check the parachute before flight.

items.name: Aircraft-type
items.desc: Medium drones. Land on landing gear, like a real aircraft.
items.why: Aircraft-type landing is an 'aircraft' method. It gives the drone a soft landing, so it is not damaged. It is effective for medium drones.
items.example: A Bayraktar TB2 lands on its gear. It is undamaged and can be launched again.
mistakes: Landing on hard surface — the drone is damaged.
Landing against the wind — the drone flips.
Landing without a check — the gear does not deploy.
items.tips: Land on flat surface. Land with the wind. Check the gear before flight.

items.name: VTOL (Vertical)
items.desc: Modern drones. Land vertically, no runway needed. Combine plane and copter.
items.why: VTOL is a 'vertical' method. It gives the drone vertical landing, so no runway is needed. It is effective for modern drones.
items.example: A VTOL drone lands vertically. It is undamaged and can be launched again.
mistakes: Landing on hard surface — the drone is damaged.
Landing against the wind — the drone flips.
Landing without a check — the engines do not start.
items.tips: Land on flat surface. Land with the wind. Check the engines before flight.

items.name: No Return
items.desc: Kamikaze. Drone explodes on target.
items.why: No return is a 'kamikaze' method. It requires no landing, so the drone explodes on the target. It is effective for strike drones.
items.example: An FPV kamikaze strikes an enemy tank. It explodes, the tank is destroyed.
mistakes: No backup guidance — the drone misses.
Ignoring accuracy — the drone misses.
No backup channel — the drone loses the target.
items.tips: Keep backup guidance. Account for accuracy. Keep a backup channel.

items.name: 433 MHz
items.desc: Long-range comms, backup channel. Less prone to interference.
items.why: 433 MHz is a 'long-range' band. It is less prone to interference, so it is effective for long-range comms. It is effective for a backup channel.
items.example: An FPV flies 10 km. The main 5.8 GHz channel is jammed, the operator switches to 433 MHz — comms return.
mistakes: Using as primary — slow.
Ignoring the antenna — weak signal.
No backup channel — loss of comms.
items.tips: Use as backup. Keep a good antenna. Switch when jammed.

items.name: 868/915 MHz
items.desc: ELRS, control. Standard for FPV drones.
items.why: 868/915 MHz is a 'standard' band. It is standard for FPV, so it is effective for control. It is effective for FPV drones.
items.example: An FPV flies 5 km. ELRS on 915 MHz gives stable comms.
mistakes: Using without ELRS — unstable comms.
Ignoring the antenna — weak signal.
No backup channel — loss of comms.
items.tips: Use ELRS. Keep a good antenna. Switch when jammed.

items.name: 1.2 GHz
items.desc: Analog video. Long-range, but poor quality.
items.why: 1.2 GHz is a 'long-range' band. It gives long-range comms but poor quality. It is effective for long-range video.
items.example: An FPV flies 10 km. Video on 1.2 GHz gives long-range comms but poor quality.
mistakes: Using as primary — poor quality.
Ignoring the antenna — weak signal.
No backup channel — loss of comms.
items.tips: Use as backup. Keep a good antenna. Switch when jammed.

items.name: 2.4 GHz
items.desc: Control, consumer band. Most common.
items.why: 2.4 GHz is a 'consumer' band. It is the most common, so it is effective for control. It is effective for most drones.
items.example: An FPV flies 5 km. Control on 2.4 GHz gives stable comms.
mistakes: Using without a check — interference.
Ignoring the antenna — weak signal.
No backup channel — loss of comms.
items.tips: Use as primary. Keep a good antenna. Switch when jammed.

items.name: 5.8 GHz
items.desc: Analog/digital video. High quality, but short range.
items.why: 5.8 GHz is a 'quality' band. It gives high quality but short range. It is effective for quality video.
items.example: An FPV flies 2 km. Video on 5.8 GHz gives high quality but short range.
mistakes: Using at long range — weak signal.
Ignoring the antenna — weak signal.
No backup channel — loss of comms.
items.tips: Use at short range. Keep a good antenna. Switch when jammed.

items.name: 6+ GHz
items.desc: Modern digital systems. EW-resistant, but expensive.
items.why: 6+ GHz is a 'resistant' band. It is EW-resistant, so it is effective for modern systems. It is effective for modern drones.
items.example: An FPV flies 5 km. Video on 6+ GHz gives stable comms even under EW.
mistakes: Using without a check — expensive.
Ignoring the antenna — weak signal.
No backup channel — loss of comms.
items.tips: Use as primary. Keep a good antenna. Switch when jammed.

items.name: MAVLink
items.desc: Telemetry protocol for autopilots (ArduPilot, PX4). Transmits coordinates, status, commands.
items.why: MAVLink is the drone's 'language' with the ground station. It transmits everything: coordinates, altitude, charge, engine status. Without it the operator does not see what the drone is doing.
items.example: The operator looks at the ground station screen. MAVLink shows: altitude 500 m, charge 60%, GPS 12 satellites. The operator sees that all is well.
mistakes: Not configuring MAVLink — the operator does not see the drone.
Ignoring telemetry — the drone falls.
No backup channel — loss of comms.
items.tips: Configure MAVLink before flight. Check telemetry. Keep a backup channel.

items.name: CRSF / ELRS
items.desc: Low-latency control protocol. Standard for FPV.
items.why: CRSF/ELRS is a 'fast' protocol. It gives low latency (10–20 ms), so the operator controls the drone in real time. It is the standard for FPV.
items.example: An FPV flies 2 km. ELRS gives 15 ms latency, the operator controls the drone in real time.
mistakes: Using without ELRS — 50+ ms latency.
Ignoring the antenna — weak signal.
No backup channel — loss of comms.
items.tips: Use ELRS. Keep a good antenna. Switch when jammed.

items.name: SBUS / PWM
items.desc: Classic protocols for servos and motors.
items.why: SBUS/PWM are 'classic' protocols. They are simple and reliable, so they are effective for servos and motors. They are the standard for most drones.
items.example: A servo is controlled by a PWM signal. It turns 90 degrees.
mistakes: Using without a check — the servo does not work.
Ignoring the wires — weak signal.
No backup channel — loss of comms.
items.tips: Check the wires. Use SBUS for many servos. Keep a backup channel.

items.name: Relay
items.desc: A relay drone lifts an antenna high and extends comms for other drones at long range.
items.why: A relay is a 'tower' of comms. It lifts the antenna high, so comms work at long range. It is effective for long missions.
items.example: An FPV flies 20 km. A relay at 500 m extends comms. The operator sees video.
mistakes: No relay — comms lost.
Ignoring altitude — weak signal.
No backup channel — loss of comms.
items.tips: Use a relay. Lift the antenna high. Keep a backup channel.

items.name: Mesh network
items.desc: Drones connect to each other and pass the signal along a chain.
items.why: Mesh is a 'network' of comms. Drones connect to each other, so the signal is passed along a chain. It is effective for group missions.
items.example: 5 FPVs fly in a group. The mesh network passes the signal from one to another. The operator sees all drones.
mistakes: No mesh — comms lost.
Ignoring distance — weak signal.
No backup channel — loss of comms.
items.tips: Use mesh for groups. Keep drones close. Keep a backup channel.

items.name: Encryption
items.desc: AES channel encryption protects against interception and command spoofing.
items.why: Encryption is a 'lock' on the channel. It protects against interception and command spoofing. It is effective for OPSEC.
items.example: An FPV flies 5 km. AES encryption protects the channel. The enemy cannot intercept video.
mistakes: No encryption — the enemy intercepts.
Using a weak key — the enemy breaks it.
No backup key — loss of comms.
items.tips: Use AES-256. Change keys. Keep a backup key.

items.name: Manual Mode
items.desc: Operator controls all axes. Requires skill, but full control.
items.why: Manual mode is 'full control'. The operator controls all axes, so he can perform complex maneuvers. It is effective for FPV.
items.example: An FPV flies in manual mode. The operator performs a flip and strikes the target.
mistakes: Flying without skill — the drone falls.
Ignoring wind — the drone drifts.
No backup mode — loss of control.
items.tips: Train in a simulator. Fly in good weather. Keep a backup mode.

items.name: Stabilization
items.desc: Drone holds horizon itself, operator sets direction. Most common mode.
items.why: Stabilization is 'assistance' to the operator. The drone holds the horizon itself, so the operator only sets direction. It is effective for most drones.
items.example: An FPV flies in stabilization mode. The operator sets direction, the drone holds the horizon.
mistakes: Flying without stabilization — the drone falls.
Ignoring wind — the drone drifts.
No backup mode — loss of control.
items.tips: Use stabilization. Fly in good weather. Keep a backup mode.

items.name: GPS Mode
items.desc: Drone holds position via satellites. Convenient for hovering and filming.
items.why: GPS mode is 'automatic hovering'. The drone holds position via satellites, so it is convenient for filming. It is effective for recon.
items.example: A Mavic flies in GPS mode. It hovers at 100 m and films video.
mistakes: Flying without GPS — the drone drifts.
Ignoring EW — GPS is jammed.
No backup mode — loss of control.
items.tips: Use GPS mode. Keep a backup mode. Account for EW.

items.name: Waypoint Navigation
items.desc: Automatic flight through set points. Operator only observes.
items.why: Waypoint is 'autopilot'. The drone flies through points automatically, so the operator only observes. It is effective for long missions.
items.example: A recon drone flies through 10 points, recording video at each. The operator only observes.
mistakes: Forgetting obstacles — the drone hits a tree.
Not checking the route — the drone flies to the enemy.
Ignoring wind — the drone drifts.
items.tips: Plan the route. Check the route. Have a backup route.

items.name: RTH (Return to Home)
items.desc: Drone flies to launch point on loss of comms or by command.
items.why: RTH is the drone's 'insurance'. If comms are lost, the drone flies home by itself. Without RTH the drone flies who-knows-where and falls.
items.example: An FPV flies to the target, suddenly comms disappear. The drone switches to RTH and flies to the launch point. The operator finds it on the ground.
mistakes: Not configuring RTH — the drone flies who-knows-where.
Configuring RTH to the wrong point — the drone flies to the enemy.
Ignoring RTH altitude — the drone may hit a tree.
items.tips: Set RTH to the launch point. Set RTH altitude above obstacles. Check RTH before flight.

items.name: Failsafe
items.desc: Behavior on loss of signal: hover, return, or land. Configured in advance.
items.why: Failsafe is the drone's 'plan B'. If signal is lost, the drone must know what to do. Without failsafe the drone simply falls.
items.example: An FPV flies, comms disappear. Failsafe is set to RTH — the drone flies home. If failsafe were 'land' — the drone would land in a field.
mistakes: Not configuring failsafe — the drone falls.
Configuring failsafe to 'land' in a forest — the drone gets stuck.
Ignoring failsafe — loss of the drone.
items.tips: Set failsafe to RTH. Check failsafe before flight. Keep a backup comm channel.

items.name: Terrain following
items.desc: Flight following terrain at a set height above ground.
items.why: Terrain following is 'terrain hugging'. The drone flies at a set height above ground, so it does not hit hills. It is effective for mountainous terrain.
items.example: A recon drone flies in mountains. Terrain following keeps 100 m above ground. The drone does not hit a hill.
mistakes: Not using terrain following — the drone hits a hill.
Ignoring the map — the drone hits a mountain.
No backup mode — loss of control.
items.tips: Use terrain following. Keep a map. Keep a backup mode.

items.name: Day Camera
items.desc: Standard for recon and FPV. Sees well by day, poorly at night and in fog.
items.why: A day camera is the drone's 'eye' by day. It sees well by day but poorly at night and in fog. It is effective for daytime recon.
items.example: An FPV flies by day. The day camera sees the target at 2 km.
mistakes: Using at night — the camera cannot see.
Ignoring fog — the camera cannot see.
No backup camera — loss of video.
items.tips: Use by day. Keep a backup camera. Account for weather.

items.name: Thermal (IR)
items.desc: Sees heat. Works at night, in smoke, through light vegetation.
items.why: A thermal imager is the drone's 'thermal eye'. It sees heat, so it works at night, in smoke, through light vegetation. It is effective for night recon.
items.example: An FPV flies at night. The thermal imager sees a tank at 1 km.
mistakes: Using by day — heat dissipates.
Ignoring camouflage — thermal sees through it.
No cooling — IR sensor overheats.
items.tips: Use at night and in bad weather. Keep cooling. Combine with a day camera.

items.name: Multispectral
items.desc: Several bands at once. For mapping and terrain analysis.
items.why: Multispectral is the drone's 'many eyes'. It sees several bands at once, so it is effective for mapping and terrain analysis.
items.example: A recon drone flies with multispectral. It sees vegetation, water, roads.
mistakes: Using without processing — data is useless.
Ignoring calibration — data is inaccurate.
No backup sensor — loss of data.
items.tips: Use for mapping. Calibrate the sensor. Keep a backup sensor.

items.name: Gimbal
items.desc: 2-3 axis mount. Keeps camera level during maneuvers.
items.why: A gimbal is the camera's 'stabilizer'. It keeps the camera level during maneuvers, so video is high quality. It is effective for recon.
items.example: A Mavic flies with a gimbal. The camera stays level, video is high quality.
mistakes: Using without a gimbal — video shakes.
Ignoring calibration — the gimbal does not work.
No backup gimbal — loss of video.
items.tips: Use a gimbal. Calibrate before flight. Keep a backup gimbal.

items.name: Night IR Illumination
items.desc: Lights up target with an infrared spotlight invisible to the eye.
items.why: IR illumination is 'invisible light'. It lights up the target with an infrared spotlight invisible to the eye. It is effective for night recon.
items.example: An FPV flies at night. IR illumination lights up the target, the thermal imager sees it.
mistakes: Using by day — invisible.
Ignoring distance — illumination is weak.
No backup illumination — loss of target.
items.tips: Use at night. Account for distance. Keep backup illumination.

items.name: LiDAR / Sonar
items.desc: Measures distance and builds a map. For mapping and obstacle avoidance.
items.why: LiDAR/sonar is a 'distance measurer'. It measures distance and builds a map, so it is effective for mapping and obstacle avoidance.
items.example: A recon drone flies with LiDAR. It builds a map of the terrain.
mistakes: Using without processing — data is useless.
Ignoring calibration — data is inaccurate.
No backup sensor — loss of data.
items.tips: Use for mapping. Calibrate the sensor. Keep a backup sensor.

items.name: Reconnaissance
items.desc: Find target, determine coordinates, pass to artillery.
items.why: Recon is the 'eyes' of artillery. It finds the target, determines coordinates, passes to artillery. It is effective for hitting targets.
items.example: A Shark flies 30 km, spots a vehicle column, transmits coordinates. Artillery covers the column.
mistakes: Flying low — you will be shot down.
Transmitting coordinates without accuracy — artillery will miss.
Forgetting about EW — GPS is jammed.
items.tips: Fly high. Transmit coordinates with 10 m accuracy. Keep a backup channel.

items.name: Correction
items.desc: Direct artillery to target, adjust fire.
items.why: Correction is 'guiding' artillery. It directs artillery to the target, adjusts fire. It is effective for hitting targets.
items.example: A Shark spots the target, transmits coordinates. Artillery fires. The Shark adjusts: 'left 50, further 100' — and confirms the kill.
mistakes: No comms with artillery — correction impossible.
Transmitting coordinates without accuracy — artillery will miss.
Forgetting about EW — GPS is jammed.
items.tips: Keep comms with artillery. Transmit coordinates with 10 m accuracy. Keep a backup channel.

items.name: Strike
items.desc: Destroy target (FPV, bomber, kamikaze).
items.why: Strike is 'destruction' of the target. It destroys the target (FPV, bomber, kamikaze). It is effective for hitting targets.
items.example: An FPV strikes an enemy tank. The tank is destroyed.
mistakes: Flying in a straight line — you will be shot down.
Ignoring EW — jamming.
No backup channel — loss of the drone.
items.tips: Attack from an unexpected angle. Keep a backup channel. Use precision guidance.

items.name: Relay
items.desc: Provide comms for other drones at long range.
items.why: Relay is a 'tower' of comms. It provides comms for other drones at long range. It is effective for long missions.
items.example: An FPV flies 20 km. A relay at 500 m extends comms.
mistakes: No relay — comms lost.
Ignoring altitude — weak signal.
No backup channel — loss of comms.
items.tips: Use a relay. Lift the antenna high. Keep a backup channel.

items.name: Swarm
items.desc: Group attack by several drones simultaneously. Hard to intercept.
items.why: Swarm is a 'group attack'. It attacks with several drones simultaneously, so it is hard to intercept. It is effective for mass attacks.
items.example: 10 FPVs fly in a swarm. They attack an enemy position simultaneously. Air defense cannot intercept all.
mistakes: No coordination — drones collide.
Ignoring EW — jamming.
No backup channel — loss of comms.
items.tips: Coordinate the swarm. Keep a backup channel. Use a mesh network.

items.name: Ambush
items.desc: Wait for target in the air (Lancet, Shahed).
items.why: Ambush is 'waiting' for the target. It waits for the target in the air (Lancet, Shahed). It is effective for hitting targets.
items.example: A Lancet circles over the road for 30 minutes until a tank appears. It dives and strikes.
mistakes: Launching without recon — the drone circles in vain.
Ignoring EW — jamming.
No backup channel — loss of the drone.
items.tips: Launch after recon. Keep a backup channel. Use optics to search for the target.

items.name: Decoy
items.desc: Distract air defense (Parody, Gerbera).
items.why: Decoy is 'distraction' of air defense. It distracts air defense (Parody, Gerbera). It is effective for mass attacks.
items.example: A Parody flies toward the city. Air defense fires at it. The real Shahed flies a different route.
mistakes: No decoy — air defense shoots down the real drone.
Ignoring EW — jamming.
No backup channel — loss of the drone.
items.tips: Use a decoy. Keep a backup channel. Coordinate with the real drone.

items.name: EW
items.desc: Jamming signals. Main passive countermeasure.
items.why: EW is 'jamming' signals. It jams GPS, video, control. It is effective for passive countermeasures.
items.example: An enemy FPV flies to the position. EW jams video. The FPV loses the target and falls.
mistakes: Jamming everything — your own drones fall too.
Ignoring frequencies — jamming does not work.
No backup channel — loss of comms.
items.tips: Jam specific frequencies. Keep a backup channel. Coordinate with your drones.

items.name: FPV Interceptors
items.desc: Ramming in the air. Sting, P1-SUN, Taras-P.
items.why: FPV interceptors are 'ramming' in the air. They ram an enemy drone. They are effective for air defense.
items.example: A Sting rams an enemy Shahed. Both drones fall.
mistakes: Ramming from close range — the explosion damages the interceptor.
Not accounting for speed — Shahed is faster.
Flying without battery reserve — you will not catch the target.
items.tips: Ram with a slight speed advantage. Keep 30% battery reserve. Work in pairs.

items.name: SAM/MANPADS
items.desc: Missiles. Expensive, but effective.
items.why: SAM/MANPADS are 'missiles' against drones. They are expensive but effective. They are effective for air defense.
items.example: A MANPADS shoots down an enemy Shahed. The missile costs $100k.
mistakes: Using against FPV — expensive.
Ignoring EW — the missile does not guide.
No missile reserve — weak air defense.
items.tips: Use against large drones. Keep a missile reserve. Account for EW.

items.name: Small Arms
items.desc: Machine guns, anti-aircraft mounts. Cheap, but low effectiveness.
items.why: Small arms are 'cheap' countermeasures. They are cheap but low effectiveness. They are effective for close-in countermeasures.
items.example: A machine gun shoots down an enemy FPV at 500 m.
mistakes: Shooting from afar — low effectiveness.
Ignoring speed — the drone is faster.
No ammo reserve — weak air defense.
items.tips: Shoot from close range. Account for speed. Keep an ammo reserve.

items.name: Nets
items.desc: Physical protection. Stretched over positions.
items.why: Nets are 'physical' protection. They are stretched over positions, so the drone gets tangled. They are effective for protecting positions.
items.example: A net is stretched over a trench. An enemy FPV gets tangled and falls.
mistakes: Not stretching the net — the drone flies through.
Ignoring distance — the net does not work.
No backup net — weak air defense.
items.tips: Stretch the net over positions. Account for distance. Keep a backup net.

items.name: Laser Weapons
items.desc: Modern systems. Burns drone with laser.
items.why: Laser weapons are 'modern' countermeasures. They burn the drone with a laser. They are effective for air defense.
items.example: A laser system burns an enemy FPV at 1 km.
mistakes: Using in fog — the laser scatters.
Ignoring power — the laser does not burn.
No backup system — weak air defense.
items.tips: Use in good weather. Account for power. Keep a backup system.

items.name: Drone Detectors
items.desc: Acoustic, RF and radar detection systems. Give time to react.
items.why: Detectors are the 'eyes' of air defense. They detect the drone at range, so they give time to react. They are effective for air defense.
items.example: An acoustic detector hears an enemy FPV at 1 km. Air defense prepares.
mistakes: Ignoring detectors — air defense is not ready.
No backup detector — weak air defense.
Ignoring noise — the detector makes mistakes.
items.tips: Use detectors. Keep a backup detector. Account for noise.

items.name: FPV
items.desc: $300–2000. Cheapest, mass-produced.
items.why: FPV is a 'mass' weapon. It is cheap, so it is expendable. One FPV costs like 1–2 grenades but can destroy a $2M tank.
items.example: A brigade buys 1000 FPVs at $500 each. Total cost: $500k. They destroy 50 tanks worth $100M. Economic benefit: 200:1.
mistakes: Buying expensive FPVs — waste of money.
Ignoring quality — a cheap FPV will not reach.
No spare FPVs — loss of tempo.
items.tips: Buy mass FPVs. Check quality. Keep a reserve.

items.name: Mavic-class
items.desc: $2000–5000. Commercial, but effective.
items.why: Mavic is a 'commercial' drone. It is more expensive than FPV but more effective for recon. It has a good camera, stabilization, GPS.
items.example: A brigade buys 50 Mavics at $3000 each. They conduct recon and correct artillery.
mistakes: Buying expensive Mavics — waste of money.
Ignoring quality — a cheap Mavic does not work.
No spare Mavics — loss of recon.
items.tips: Buy proven Mavics. Check quality. Keep a reserve.

items.name: Recon
items.desc: $5000–50 000. Leleka, Shark, Furia.
items.why: Recon is the 'eyes' of the brigade. It is more expensive than Mavic but more effective for recon. It flies high, sees far, corrects artillery.
items.example: A brigade buys 5 Lelekas at $20k each. They conduct recon at 30 km.
mistakes: Buying expensive recon — waste of money.
Ignoring quality — a cheap recon does not work.
No spare recon — loss of recon.
items.tips: Buy proven recon. Check quality. Keep a reserve.

items.name: Attack
items.why: Attack is the 'sword' of the brigade. It is more expensive than recon but more effective for strikes. It carries munitions, strikes targets.
items.example: A brigade buys 2 Bayraktar TB2s at $50k each. They strike enemy columns.
mistakes: Buying expensive attack — waste of money.
Ignoring quality — a cheap attack does not work.
No spare attack — loss of tempo.
items.tips: Buy proven attack. Check quality. Keep a reserve.

items.name: Heavy Kamikaze
items.desc: $30 000–200 000. Shahed, Lancet.
items.why: Heavy kamikaze is a 'strategic' weapon. It is more expensive than FPV but more effective for long strikes. It flies 1000+ km, strikes targets.
items.example: A brigade buys 10 Shaheds at $100k each. They strike enemy depots.
mistakes: Buying expensive kamikaze — waste of money.
Ignoring quality — a cheap kamikaze will not reach.
No spare kamikaze — loss of tempo.
items.tips: Buy proven kamikaze. Check quality. Keep a reserve.

items.name: Strategic
items.desc: $1M+. Cruise and ballistic missiles.
items.why: Strategic is a 'strategic' weapon. It is expensive but effective for strategic strikes. It flies 1000+ km, strikes strategic targets.
items.example: A brigade buys 2 cruise missiles at $1M each. They strike enemy bases.
mistakes: Buying expensive strategic — waste of money.
Ignoring quality — a cheap missile will not reach.
No spare missiles — loss of tempo.
items.tips: Buy proven missiles. Check quality. Keep a reserve.

items.name: Speed
items.desc: Cruise and max, km/h. Affects time to target and interception capability.
items.why: Speed is the drone's 'tempo'. It affects time to target and interception capability. The faster the drone, the harder it is to intercept.
items.example: An FPV flies 100 km/h. It reaches the target in 2 minutes. Shahed flies 200 km/h — in 1 minute.
mistakes: Ignoring speed — the drone will not reach.
No speed reserve — loss of tempo.
Ignoring wind — the drone drifts.
items.tips: Account for speed. Keep a reserve. Account for wind.

items.name: Flight Altitude
items.desc: Working and max, m. Determines visibility and air defense engagement zone.
items.why: Altitude is the drone's 'visibility'. It determines visibility and air defense engagement zone. The higher the drone, the further it sees, but the easier it is to detect.
items.example: An FPV flies at 100 m — radar does not see it, but optics do. Shahed flies at 1000 m — radar sees it.
mistakes: Flying low — you will be shot down.
Flying high — you will be detected.
Ignoring terrain — the drone hits the ground.
items.tips: Account for altitude. Keep a reserve. Account for terrain.

items.name: Endurance
items.desc: How long the drone can fly without refueling. Key metric for recon.
items.why: Endurance is the drone's 'stamina'. It shows how long the drone can fly without refueling. The higher the endurance, the longer the drone stays in the air.
items.example: A Leleka flies 4 hours. It conducts recon for 4 hours. An FPV flies 15 minutes — 15 minutes.
mistakes: Ignoring endurance — the drone falls.
No fuel reserve — the drone will not reach.
Ignoring wind — endurance decreases.
items.tips: Account for endurance. Keep a reserve. Account for wind.

items.name: Payload
items.desc: Mass of warhead or sensors, kg. Determines strike power.
items.why: Payload is the drone's 'power'. It determines strike power. The larger the payload, the larger the warhead or sensors.
items.example: An FPV carries 1 kg of warhead. It strikes infantry. Baba Yaga carries 10 kg — strikes a bunker.
mistakes: Overloading the drone — it falls.
No payload reserve — loss of tempo.
Ignoring weight — the drone does not take off.
items.tips: Account for payload. Keep a reserve. Account for weight.

items.name: Deployment Time
items.desc: From box to takeoff. Important for rapid response.
items.why: Deployment time is the 'speed' of reaction. It shows how much time is needed from box to takeoff. The shorter, the faster the reaction.
items.example: An FPV deploys in 2 minutes. It reacts quickly to a target. A Leleka deploys in 10 minutes — slower.
mistakes: Ignoring deployment time — loss of tempo.
No spare drone — loss of tempo.
Ignoring weather — deployment is delayed.
items.tips: Account for deployment time. Keep a reserve. Account for weather.

items.name: Crew
items.desc: Number of operators (pilot, camera operator, commander).
items.why: Crew is the drone's 'team'. It shows how many operators are needed. The larger the crew, the more complex the mission.
items.example: An FPV is controlled by 1 operator. A Bayraktar TB2 is controlled by 3 operators: pilot, camera operator, commander.
mistakes: Ignoring crew — the mission fails.
No spare crew — loss of tempo.
Ignoring skills — the crew makes mistakes.
items.tips: Account for crew. Keep a reserve. Train the crew.

items.name: Wind
items.desc: Limits: FPV — up to 10 m/s, Mavic — up to 8 m/s, large — up to 15 m/s. Strong wind drifts and drains battery.
items.why: Wind is the main enemy of FPV. At 10 m/s the drone drifts 1 m per second of flight, and the battery drains 30–50% faster. At 100 m altitude the wind is stronger than on the ground — this is called 'wind shear'.
items.example: The operator launches an FPV in 8 m/s wind. The drone flies 2 km to the target, but the wind drifts it 200 m sideways. The operator corrects course, but the battery drains faster — the drone does not reach. Conclusion: in 8+ m/s wind, plan shorter distances.
mistakes: Ignoring wind at altitude — calm on the ground, but 12 m/s at 100 m.
Flying against the wind on the return — battery will not last.
Launching a light drone in gusts — it will flip.
items.tips: Check wind at different altitudes (recon drone or anemometer). Plan 30% battery reserve for the return against the wind. In gusts >12 m/s — do not fly.

items.name: Precipitation
items.desc: Rain and snow degrade video and can short electronics. Most drones are not waterproof.
items.why: Precipitation is the 'killer' of electronics. Rain and snow degrade video and can short electronics. Most drones are not waterproof.
items.example: An FPV flies in rain. Water gets into the electronics, the drone falls. Conclusion: do not fly in rain.
mistakes: Flying in rain — the drone shorts.
Ignoring snow — the drone freezes.
No waterproof drone — loss of the drone.
items.tips: Do not fly in rain. Use waterproof drones. Keep a spare drone.

items.name: Temperature
items.desc: Frost reduces battery capacity by 20–40%. Heat overheats electronics.
items.why: Temperature is the 'enemy' of the battery. Frost reduces capacity by 20–40%. Heat overheats electronics. Both factors shorten flight time.
items.example: Winter, -5°C. The operator takes a charged battery from a warm room, but while the drone flies, the battery cools and drains twice as fast. The drone does not reach the target. Conclusion: keep batteries in a thermal bag and charge right before flight.
mistakes: Charging a cold battery — it will not charge fully.
Leaving the battery in the sun — overheating and degradation.
Flying in heat without checking ESC temperature.
items.tips: Keep batteries in a thermal bag. Charge at room temperature. In heat, pause between flights to cool down.

items.name: Fog
items.desc: Degrades optics and comms. Thermal works better than day camera.
items.why: Fog is the 'enemy' of optics. It degrades optics and comms. Thermal works better than a day camera.
items.example: An FPV flies in fog. The day camera cannot see the target. The thermal imager sees the target at 500 m.
mistakes: Flying in fog with a day camera — you cannot see the target.
Ignoring comms — weak signal.
No thermal — loss of target.
items.tips: Use a thermal imager. Keep a backup channel. Account for weather.

items.name: Turbulence
items.desc: Dangerous at low altitudes and near buildings. Can flip a light drone.
items.why: Turbulence is a 'danger' at low altitudes. It can flip a light drone. It is effective for losing the drone.
items.example: An FPV flies near a building. Turbulence flips the drone. The drone falls.
mistakes: Flying near buildings — turbulence.
Ignoring wind — turbulence.
No spare drone — loss of the drone.
items.tips: Fly away from buildings. Account for wind. Keep a spare drone.

items.name: LiPo
items.desc: Most common for FPV. High current output, but sensitive to over-discharge and fire-prone.
items.why: LiPo is the 'energy' of FPV. It gives high current output but is sensitive to over-discharge and fire-prone. It is effective for FPV.
items.example: An FPV flies with LiPo. It gives 100A current. The drone flies 15 minutes.
mistakes: Over-discharging LiPo — it will explode.
Charging unattended — fire.
Storing at 0% — degradation.
items.tips: Do not over-discharge. Charge under supervision. Store at 3.8 V per cell.

items.name: Li-Ion
items.desc: Higher capacity per unit weight. For recon and long flights.
items.why: Li-Ion is the 'energy' of recon. It gives higher capacity per unit weight, so it is effective for long flights. It is effective for recon.
items.example: A Leleka flies with Li-Ion. It flies 4 hours.
mistakes: Over-discharging Li-Ion — it will explode.
Charging unattended — fire.
Storing at 0% — degradation.
items.tips: Do not over-discharge. Charge under supervision. Store at 3.8 V per cell.

items.name: C-rate
items.desc: Max discharge current rating. FPV needs high (50C+).
items.why: C-rate is the battery's 'power'. It shows max discharge current. FPV needs high (50C+), otherwise the drone will not take off.
items.example: An FPV with LiPo 50C gives 100A current. The drone flies. An FPV with LiPo 10C gives 20A — the drone will not take off.
mistakes: Using low C-rate — the drone will not take off.
Ignoring C-rate — the drone falls.
No spare battery — loss of tempo.
items.tips: Use 50C+ for FPV. Account for C-rate. Keep a reserve.

items.name: Field Charging
items.desc: Generators, solar panels, car inverters. Plan charging in advance.
items.why: Field charging is 'energy' in combat. It allows charging batteries in the field. It is effective for long missions.
items.example: The operator charges LiPo from a generator. He charges 10 batteries in 2 hours.
mistakes: No generator — batteries drain.
Ignoring weather — the solar panel does not work.
No backup charging — loss of tempo.
items.tips: Keep a generator. Use solar panels. Keep backup charging.

items.name: Storage
items.desc: Store LiPo at 3.8 V per cell, in a fireproof bag, away from moisture.
items.why: Storage is the 'safety' of the battery. It protects against fire and degradation. It is effective for long storage.
items.example: The operator stores LiPo at 3.8 V in a fireproof bag. The battery does not degrade.
mistakes: Storing at 0% — degradation.
Storing at 100% — fire.
Storing without a bag — fire.
items.tips: Store at 3.8 V. Use a fireproof bag. Keep away from moisture.

items.name: Maintenance Schedule
items.desc: Before flight — inspect props, motors, antennas. After — clean, check mounts.
items.why: Maintenance is the 'check' of the drone. It protects against crashes. It is effective for a long drone life.
items.example: The operator checks the props before flight. He sees a crack and replaces the prop. The drone does not fall.
mistakes: Not checking — the drone falls.
Ignoring cracks — the drone falls.
No spare parts — loss of tempo.
items.tips: Check before flight. Keep spare parts. Clean after flight.

items.name: Common Faults
items.desc: Worn props, overheated motors, damaged ESCs, torn antennas.
items.why: Common faults are the 'enemy' of the drone. They lead to crashes. They are effective for losing the drone.
items.example: The operator sees an overheated motor. He replaces the motor. The drone does not fall.
mistakes: Ignoring faults — the drone falls.
No spare parts — loss of tempo.
Not checking — the drone falls.
items.tips: Check for faults. Keep spare parts. Clean after flight.

items.name: Modularity
items.desc: Most FPVs are built from modules — frame, motors, ESC, camera, VTX. Easy to replace.
items.why: Modularity is the 'repair' of the drone. It allows easy replacement of modules. It is effective for a long drone life.
items.example: The operator replaces the ESC in 5 minutes. The drone flies again.
mistakes: No spare modules — loss of tempo.
Ignoring modularity — repair is slow.
Not checking modules — the drone falls.
items.tips: Keep spare modules. Use modular drones. Check modules.

items.name: Diagnostics
items.desc: Check flight logs, telemetry, cell voltage. Logs show the cause of a crash.
items.why: Diagnostics is the 'analysis' of the drone. It shows the cause of a crash. It is effective for a long drone life.
items.example: The operator analyzes the logs. He sees that the ESC overheated. He replaces the ESC.
mistakes: Not analyzing logs — the crash repeats.
Ignoring telemetry — the drone falls.
Not checking voltage — the battery explodes.
items.tips: Analyze logs. Check telemetry. Check voltage.

items.name: Simulators
items.desc: Velocidrone, Liftoff, DCL. Safely practice maneuvers without risking a drone.
items.why: Simulators are the 'training' of the operator. They allow safe practice of maneuvers. They are effective for beginners.
items.example: The operator trains in Velocidrone for 10 hours. He learns to do a flip. In reality he does not lose the drone.
mistakes: Not training — the drone falls.
Ignoring the simulator — loss of the drone.
No spare drone — loss of tempo.
items.tips: Train in a simulator. Use realistic settings. Keep a spare drone.

items.name: Basic Maneuvers
items.desc: Takeoff, landing, hover, turns, circling. Foundation for a beginner.
items.why: Basic maneuvers are the 'foundation' of flight. They allow controlling the drone. They are effective for beginners.
items.example: The operator learns takeoff, landing, hover. He controls the drone.
mistakes: Not training basic maneuvers — the drone falls.
Ignoring maneuvers — loss of the drone.
No spare drone — loss of tempo.
items.tips: Train basic maneuvers. Use a simulator. Keep a spare drone.

items.name: Advanced Maneuvers
items.desc: Flips, rolls, split-S, indoor flight. For experienced pilots.
items.why: Advanced maneuvers are 'advanced' flight. They allow complex tricks. They are effective for experienced pilots.
items.example: The operator performs a flip. He strikes the target from an unexpected angle.
mistakes: Not training advanced maneuvers — the drone falls.
Ignoring maneuvers — loss of the drone.
No spare drone — loss of tempo.
items.tips: Train advanced maneuvers. Use a simulator. Keep a spare drone.

items.name: Safety Rules
items.desc: Survey the area, keep distance from people, never fly over crowds.
items.why: Safety rules are the 'protection' of people. They protect against crashes. They are effective for safety.
items.example: The operator surveys the area. He sees people and does not fly over them.
mistakes: Not surveying the area — the drone falls on people.
Ignoring distance — the drone falls on people.
Flying over crowds — the drone falls on people.
items.tips: Survey the area. Keep distance. Do not fly over crowds.

items.name: Position Masking
items.desc: Don't launch from open terrain, change launch points.
items.why: Masking is the 'protection' of the operator. It protects against detection. It is effective for OPSEC.
items.example: The operator launches the drone from cover. The enemy does not see him.
mistakes: Launching from open terrain — you will be seen.
Not changing launch points — you will be detected.
Ignoring masking — you will be killed.
items.tips: Launch from cover. Change launch points. Use masking.

items.name: Radio Silence
items.desc: Minimum transmissions, phone off, no extra signals.
items.why: Radio silence is the 'protection' against detection. It protects against interception. It is effective for OPSEC.
items.example: The operator turns off the phone. He does not transmit extra signals.
mistakes: Not turning off the phone — you will be detected.
Transmitting extra signals — you will be detected.
Ignoring radio silence — you will be killed.
items.tips: Turn off the phone. Minimum transmissions. Use radio silence.

items.name: Digital Hygiene
items.desc: Don't publish photos/videos with geolocation, don't dump logs to public clouds.
items.why: Digital hygiene is the 'protection' of data. It protects against detection. It is effective for OPSEC.
items.example: The operator does not publish photos with geolocation. The enemy does not see his position.
mistakes: Publishing photos with geolocation — you will be detected.
Dumping logs to clouds — you will be detected.
Ignoring hygiene — you will be killed.
items.tips: Do not publish photos with geolocation. Do not dump logs. Use digital hygiene.

items.name: Interception Protection
items.desc: Channel encryption, backup frequencies, avoid pattern frequencies.
items.why: Interception protection is the 'protection' of the channel. It protects against interception. It is effective for OPSEC.
items.example: The operator uses AES encryption. The enemy does not intercept video.
mistakes: No encryption — the enemy intercepts.
Using pattern frequencies — the enemy jams.
Ignoring protection — you will be detected.
items.tips: Use AES encryption. Keep backup frequencies. Avoid pattern frequencies.

items.name: Battery Charge
items.desc: Check that battery is charged. Better to have spare.
items.why: Charge is the drone's 'energy'. It protects against falling. It is effective for a long flight.
items.example: The operator checks the charge. Battery 100%. The drone flies.
mistakes: Not checking charge — the drone falls.
Ignoring the reserve — loss of tempo.
No spare battery — loss of tempo.
items.tips: Check charge. Keep a reserve. Charge before flight.

items.name: GPS/Comms Check
items.desc: Make sure satellites are found, comms stable.
items.why: GPS/comms are the drone's 'eyes'. They protect against loss. They are effective for a long flight.
items.example: The operator checks GPS. 12 satellites. Comms stable. The drone flies.
mistakes: Not checking GPS — the drone falls.
Ignoring comms — loss of the drone.
No backup channel — loss of comms.
items.tips: Check GPS. Check comms. Keep a backup channel.

items.name: Camera Check
items.desc: Check that video is transmitted, optics clean.
items.why: The camera is the drone's 'eye'. It protects against losing the target. It is effective for recon.
items.example: The operator checks the camera. Video is transmitted. Optics are clean. The drone flies.
mistakes: Not checking the camera — loss of target.
Ignoring optics — loss of target.
No backup camera — loss of video.
items.tips: Check the camera. Clean optics. Keep a backup camera.

items.name: Weather Conditions
items.desc: Wind, rain, temperature. Don't fly in strong wind.
items.why: Weather is the drone's 'enemy'. It protects against crashes. It is effective for a long flight.
items.example: The operator checks the weather. Wind 5 m/s. The drone flies.
mistakes: Ignoring weather — the drone falls.
Flying in rain — the drone shorts.
No spare drone — loss of tempo.
items.tips: Check the weather. Do not fly in rain. Keep a spare drone.

items.name: Flight Plan
items.desc: Know where you fly, where target is, how to return.
items.why: The flight plan is the 'map' of the flight. It protects against loss. It is effective for a long flight.
items.example: The operator plans the route. He knows where he flies, where the target is, how to return.
mistakes: Not planning the route — the drone falls.
Ignoring the target — loss of tempo.
No backup route — loss of the drone.
items.tips: Plan the route. Know the target. Have a backup route.

items.name: Backup Frequency
items.desc: Have backup comm channel in case main is jammed.
items.why: A backup frequency is the 'insurance' of comms. It protects against jamming. It is effective for a long flight.
items.example: The operator has a backup frequency. The main channel is jammed, he switches to backup.
mistakes: No backup frequency — loss of comms.
Ignoring jamming — loss of the drone.
No backup channel — loss of comms.
items.tips: Keep a backup frequency. Switch when jammed. Keep a backup channel.

items.name: Return Point
items.desc: Make sure auto-return is configured correctly.
items.why: The return point is the drone's 'insurance'. It protects against loss. It is effective for a long flight.
items.example: The operator checks RTH. It is set to the launch point. The drone flies.
mistakes: Not configuring RTH — the drone flies who-knows-where.
Ignoring RTH — loss of the drone.
No backup RTH — loss of the drone.
items.tips: Configure RTH. Check RTH. Keep a backup RTH.

items.name: Loss of Comms
items.desc: Drone has auto-return to base. Don't panic.
items.why: Loss of comms is the operator's 'fear'. It protects against loss. It is effective for a long flight.
items.example: An FPV flies, comms disappear. The drone switches to RTH and flies to the launch point. The operator finds it on the ground.
mistakes: Panicking — the drone falls.
No RTH — the drone flies who-knows-where.
No backup channel — loss of comms.
items.tips: Do not panic. Keep RTH. Keep a backup channel.

items.name: GPS Loss
items.desc: Switch to inertial navigation. Drone will continue flight.
items.why: GPS loss is the operator's 'fear'. It protects against loss. It is effective for a long flight.
items.example: An FPV flies, GPS disappears. The drone switches to INS and continues flight. The operator corrects by video.
mistakes: Panicking — the drone falls.
No INS — the drone falls.
No backup channel — loss of comms.
items.tips: Do not panic. Keep INS. Keep a backup channel.

items.name: Capture by Enemy FPV
items.desc: Evasive maneuver. Sharp change in altitude and course.
items.why: Capture is the operator's 'fear'. It protects against loss. It is effective for a long flight.
items.example: An enemy FPV attacks. The operator performs a sharp maneuver. The enemy FPV misses.
mistakes: Not maneuvering — the drone falls.
Ignoring capture — loss of the drone.
No spare drone — loss of tempo.
items.tips: Maneuver. Change altitude and course. Keep a spare drone.

items.name: EW Jamming
items.desc: Switch to backup frequency or auto-return.
items.why: EW jamming is the operator's 'fear'. It protects against loss. It is effective for a long flight.
items.example: An FPV flies, EW jams video. The operator switches to backup frequency. Video returns.
mistakes: Panicking — the drone falls.
No backup frequency — loss of comms.
No RTH — the drone flies who-knows-where.
items.tips: Do not panic. Switch frequency. Keep RTH.

items.name: Engine Failure
items.desc: Glide to target. For kamikaze — this is normal.
items.why: Engine failure is the operator's 'fear'. It protects against loss. It is effective for a long flight.
items.example: An FPV flies, the engine fails. The drone glides to the target and explodes.
mistakes: Panicking — the drone falls.
No spare drone — loss of tempo.
Ignoring failure — loss of the drone.
items.tips: Do not panic. Glide to target. Keep a spare drone.

items.name: Battery Fire
items.desc: Don't extinguish with water. Use sand or a fireproof bag.
items.why: Battery fire is a 'danger' to the operator. It protects against explosion. It is effective for safety.
items.example: The drone falls, the battery is damaged and starts smoking. The operator throws it in sand and covers it. After 5 minutes the smoke stops.
mistakes: Extinguishing with water — explosion and sparks.
Keeping a damaged battery in a pocket — fire on the body.
Leaving the battery unattended — it ignites in 10–30 minutes.
items.tips: Always have sand or a fireproof bag at hand. A damaged battery — into sand, in the open air, away from people. Do not leave unattended for 30 minutes.
